speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder; to begin, are you currently experiencing any tremors, stiffness, or involuntary movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; given the new onset movement disorder after starting risperidone, does the movement feel like a rhythmic shaking (tremor), a repetitive twisting motion (dystonia), or a writhing sensation (chorea)? Also, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or stiffness in your jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The symptoms you describe—inability to remain still, fidgeting, and leg pacing—are classic signs of akathisia. Given your recent start on risperidone, this is a likely medication side effect. Has this restlessness been present since starting the medication, and have you noticed any worsening of this feeling throughout the day?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia

The normal lab results rule out metabolic causes, and your history of recent risperidone initiation combined with symptoms like an inability to remain still and leg pacing is classic for akathisia. Do you feel that this internal restlessness is significantly worsening your sleep or daily functioning?
